q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of a vehicle headlamp?
title: Vehicle headlamp carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the polycarbonate lens, housing, reflector and electronics per lamp and multiply by supplier figures. Add moulding, coating, metallising and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by lamps made.

ul: Polycarbonate lens and PP or other plastic housing.
Bulbs or LED modules, wiring and connectors.
Hard coating the lens and vacuum metallising the reflector.

p: Report per lamp by vehicle type. LED modules add electronics that a bulb lamp does not have.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 85,200 / 60,000 = 1.420 kg CO2 per unit
Add plastics, reflector and lighting parts for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
